5	/// Read-only rendered-Markdown view (preview mode of the file viewer). Hosts a `WKWebView` that
6	/// loads a bundled offline template (`Resources/markdown/template.html`) and drives it with the
7	/// file's Markdown source. Unlike the old `NSAttributedString` renderer this supports GFM **tables**,
8	/// task lists, and **mermaid diagrams** — the page runs bundled `marked` + `DOMPurify` + `mermaid`,
9	/// all `file:`-local with a strict CSP, so nothing reaches the network.
10	///
11	/// The Markdown is untrusted workroom content, so it is defended in depth: DOMPurify strips any
12	/// executable HTML before it hits the DOM, the CSP blocks remote script/connect/frame loads, and the
13	/// navigation delegate lets only `http`/`https`/`mailto` links open (in the user's browser) — every
14	/// other scheme, and any attempt to navigate the frame away from the template, is dropped.
15	struct MarkdownWebView: NSViewRepresentable {
16	  /// The raw Markdown source to render.
17	  let markdown: String
18	  let tokens: ThemeTokens
19	  /// The theme generation; a change recolours the page (CSS variables + mermaid theme) in place.
20	  let generation: Int
21	  /// Called once, on the main actor, when the first Markdown render has actually *painted*.
22	  ///
23	  /// Booting the page is not instant — the bundled scripts are ~3.5 MB (mermaid alone is 3.4 MB and
24	  /// ~104 ms of the ~117 ms script parse), on top of spawning a fresh WebContent process. Until
25	  /// `didFinish` lands and `__render` runs, the web view is an empty themed rectangle, which read as
26	  /// "the panel is blank for a short while". The owner uses this to cover that window with a loader.
27	  var onFirstRender: () -> Void = {}
28	
29	  /// The bundled template and the directory the web assets live in (read-access scope for the load).
30	  private static let assetDirectory = Bundle.main.url(
31	    forResource: "markdown", withExtension: nil, subdirectory: nil)
32	  private static let templateURL = assetDirectory?.appendingPathComponent("template.html")
33	
34	  func makeCoordinator() -> Coordinator { Coordinator() }
35	
36	  func makeNSView(context: Context) -> WKWebView {
37	    let config = WKWebViewConfiguration()
38	    config.websiteDataStore = .nonPersistent()  // no cache/cookies for untrusted content
39	    // Seed the theme CSS variables at document start, before styles.css first paints. Without this
40	    // the page paints one frame with the stylesheet's light `--bg` default (a white flash over the
41	    // panel in dark mode) until `didFinish`'s applyTheme lands. Setting them pre-paint themes frame 1.
42	    if let boot = Self.themeBootScript(themeVars(tokens)) {
43	      config.userContentController.addUserScript(boot)
44	    }
45	
46	    let webView = WKWebView(frame: .zero, configuration: config)
47	    webView.navigationDelegate = context.coordinator
48	    webView.setValue(false, forKey: "drawsBackground")  // let the page's themed background show
49	    webView.underPageBackgroundColor = tokens.nsBg  // no white flash before first paint
50	    context.coordinator.webView = webView
51	    context.coordinator.templateURL = Self.templateURL
52	    context.coordinator.assetDirectory = Self.assetDirectory
53	    context.coordinator.onFirstRender = onFirstRender
54	
55	    if let template = Self.templateURL, let dir = Self.assetDirectory {
56	      webView.loadFileURL(template, allowingReadAccessTo: dir)
57	    }
58	    context.coordinator.pendingMarkdown = markdown
59	    context.coordinator.pendingThemeVars = themeVars(tokens)
60	    return webView
61	  }

64	    webView.underPageBackgroundColor = tokens.nsBg

66	    coordinator.onFirstRender = onFirstRender  // the closure captures a fresh view each update

98	  private static func themeBootScript(_ vars: [String: String]) -> WKUserScript? {

100	      let json = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
101	    else { return nil }
102	    let source = """
103	      (function () {

113	  private static func css(_ color: NSColor) -> String {
114	    guard let c = color.usingColorSpace(.sRGB) else { return "rgba(128,128,128,1)" }
115	    let r = Int((c.redComponent * 255).rounded())
116	    let g = Int((c.greenComponent * 255).rounded())
117	    let b = Int((c.blueComponent * 255).rounded())
118	    let a = String(format: "%.3f", c.alphaComponent)

210	    private func reportFirstRender() {

227	    /// Gate navigations. The initial template load (and in-page `#anchor` scrolls) stay in the frame;
228	    /// a clicked link opens externally only for allowlisted schemes; everything else is dropped.
229	    func webView(
230	      _ webView: WKWebView, decidePolicyFor navigationAction: WKNavigationAction,
231	      decisionHandler: @escaping (WKNavigationActionPolicy) -> Void
232	    ) {
233	      switch Self.navigationDecision(
234	        url: navigationAction.request.url,
235	        isLinkActivated: navigationAction.navigationType == .linkActivated,
236	        templateURL: templateURL, assetDirectory: assetDirectory)
237	      {
238	      case .allow:
239	        decisionHandler(.allow)
240	      case .openExternally(let url):

243	      case .cancel:

251	    static func navigationDecision(

253	    ) -> NavigationDecision {
254	      guard let url else { return .cancel }
255	      if !isLinkActivated {

257	        return isBundledAsset(url, assetDirectory: assetDirectory) ? .allow : .cancel
258	      }
259	      // In-page anchor: same file, differing only by fragment — allow the scroll.
260	      if url.isFileURL, let template = templateURL,
261	        url.deletingFragment() == template.deletingFragment()
262	      {
263	        return .allow
264	      }
265	      // A real outbound link opens in the user's browser, but only for web/mail schemes.

DESIGN A FIX PLAN for a production App Hang (Sentry WORKROOM-2B, "App hanging for at least 2000 ms", Workroom Nightly build).

Evidence — main-thread sample at hang detection:
dyld start → SwiftUI App.main → NSApplication run → CFRunLoop observer → NSHostingView.beginTransaction → GraphHost.flushTransactions/runTransaction → AttributeGraph Subgraph::update → DynamicBody.updateValue → ViewBodyAccessor.updateBody → closure in ViewBodyAccessor.updateBody → 3 unsymbolicated "Workroom Nightly" frames → Foundation `String.init(format:)` → withVaList → +[NSString _stringWithValidatedFormat:…] → CoreFoundation __CFStringAppendFormatCore → __CFStringAppendBytes → __CFStringChangeSizeMultiple.

Established facts from exploration (verified, treat as given):
- Only two production `String(format:)` sites exist in the app: macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/Avatar.swift:55 (`Insecure.MD5.hash(...).map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()` inside `AvatarSubject.gravatar(email:pixelSize:)`, called from `AvatarSubject.init(author:pixelSize:)` at Avatar.swift:28/32) and macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/MarkdownWebView.swift:118 (`css()` → `themeVars()`, only on the NSViewRepresentable make/update path, `body` is Never — not a ViewBodyAccessor path). A third, macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift:250 `hexColor`, has zero callers.
- The matching chain: `HistoryRow.body` (macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/HistoryPanel.swift:177) builds avatars inline at HistoryPanel.swift:212-213: `AvatarStack(subjects: commit.authors.map { AvatarSubject(author: $0, pixelSize: 48) }, size: 16)`. 16 `String(format: "%02x")` calls per author, per row, per body pass. Nothing caches an AvatarSubject anywhere (4 construction sites: HistoryPanel.swift:213, HistoryPanel.swift:458 in HistoryCommitCard, ChangesetDetailView.swift:156, PullRequestPanel.swift:149-150 — the last takes the non-MD5 `init(reviewer:)` branch).
- Amplifier 1: HistoryPanel.swift:79-81 uses an EAGER `VStack` inside a `ScrollView` over `model.commits` — every loaded row's body is built, on-screen or not. Other panels in the app already use `LazyVStack` (ScriptLogContent.swift:68, ThemePicker.swift:62, CommitSheet.swift:177, OpenWorkroomDialog.swift:89, NewWorkroomDialog.swift:62). DiffViewer.swift:366 is deliberately eager (bounded at 2000 lines) — that comment explains why lazy was rejected THERE.
- Amplifier 2: `HistoryRow` (HistoryPanel.swift:150-176) holds `@EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore` and `@ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions`, used ONLY by its `isSelected` computed property (HistoryPanel.swift:345-352: `store.selectedTarget` + `sessions.focusedTab(for:)` → `.changeset(descriptor).commitID == commit.commitID`), and it passes `sessions` down to `DivergentSiblingRow`. It's also non-elidable (a non-Equatable `open:` closure). So EVERY AppStore or TerminalSessions publish re-runs EVERY row's body. `TerminalSessions.updateTitle` reassigns `@Published tabsByTarget` (Core/TerminalSessions.swift:947) and `pulsePaneActivity` bumps `@Published activityPulses` (:940) — these fire at high frequency while an agent streams in a terminal.
- Amplifier 3: window size is unbounded — Core/HistoryModel.swift:42 `pageSize = 100`, `:89 loadMore` → `commits.count + pageSize` with no cap, `:69 refresh` → `max(pageSize, commits.count)` so the grown window persists.

# Fix Sentry WORKROOM-2B — 2-second App Hang in the History pane

## Context

Sentry issue **WORKROOM-2B** ("App Hanging: App hanging for at least 2000 ms.", Workroom Nightly,
event `69501d5f939e4fd9896caa31f8501ba5`). The main-thread sample taken at hang detection:

```
NSHostingView.beginTransaction → GraphHost.flushTransactions → AG::Subgraph::update
  → DynamicBody.updateValue → ViewBodyAccessor.updateBody
    → [3 Workroom Nightly frames, unsymbolicated]
      → Foundation String.init(format:) → +[NSString _stringWithValidatedFormat:…]
        → __CFStringAppendFormatCore → __CFStringAppendBytes → __CFStringChangeSizeMultiple
```

So a SwiftUI `body` calls `String(format:)` within ~3 hops, and that pass held the main thread ≥2 s.
The app has exactly **two** production `String(format:)` sites; only one is reachable from a `body`:

```
HistoryRow.body                      Views/HistoryPanel.swift:177 (avatars at :212-213)
 └ authors.map { … }                 Views/HistoryPanel.swift:213
   └ AvatarSubject.init(author:)      Views/Avatar.swift:28 → :32
     └ gravatar(email:pixelSize:)     Views/Avatar.swift:51
       └ String(format: "%02x", $0)   Views/Avatar.swift:55   ← 16 calls per author, per row, per pass
```

(`MarkdownWebView.swift:118` is the other site, but its `body` is `Never` — it runs on the
`NSViewRepresentable` update path, not `ViewBodyAccessor`. `GhosttyApp.swift:250 hexColor` has no callers.)

One sample doesn't prove the format calls *are* the 2 s — three factors multiply, and the fix has to
address all three:

1. **Cost per call.** 16 full format-string parses + a CFString realloc per author, to produce 32 hex
   characters, plus MD5 + a `URL(string:)` parse. Nothing is cached — `AvatarSubject` is built fresh
   at all 4 construction sites, every pass.
2. **Rows built per pass.** `HistoryPanel.swift:80` is an **eager** `VStack` inside a `ScrollView`, so
   every loaded row's body is built whether visible or not (other panels already use `LazyVStack`:
   `ScriptLogContent.swift:68`, `ThemePicker.swift:62`, `CommitSheet.swift:177`).
3. **Passes per second.** `HistoryRow` holds `@EnvironmentObject store` + `@ObservedObject sessions`
   (`HistoryPanel.swift:157`/`:160`) used *only* by `isSelected` (`:346-353`), and is non-elidable (a
   non-`Equatable` `open:` closure). `TerminalSessions.updateTitle` (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:947`)
   and `pulsePaneActivity` (`:940`) reassign `@Published` state per terminal output burst — so while an
   agent streams, **every** publish re-runs **every** row's body. Window size is unbounded
   (`HistoryModel.swift:42/89/69`): 500 commits × 2 authors × 16 ≈ 16 000 format calls per publish.

Secondary: the report's app frames came back **unsymbolicated**. Nightly *does* emit dSYMs
(`dwarf-with-dsym`) and `macapp/Scripts/release.sh:110-120` *does* have a `sentry-cli debug-files
upload` step, but `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:141` never installs `sentry-cli` and its build step
(`:162-174`) passes no `SENTRY_*` secrets — so the upload silently skips every night. Nightly also
reports `environment: "production"` (`Core/SentryConfig.swift:27-33`), making nightly hangs
indistinguishable from real-release ones.

Outcome: the History pane costs work proportional to *visible* rows that *changed*, not to the whole
loaded window on every terminal keystroke — and the next nightly hang arrives symbolicated.

---

## Step 0 — Symbolication + environment (lands first, independent)

- **`.github/workflows/nightly.yml:141`** — add `getsentry/tools/sentry-cli` to the `brew install`
  line (mirroring `release.yml:62`).
- **`.github/workflows/nightly.yml:162-174`** — add to the build step's `env:` the three vars
  `release.sh:110` gates on, exactly as `release.yml:97-99` does: `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`,
  `SENTRY_PROJECT` from secrets.
- **`macapp/Scripts/release.sh:116`/`:119`** — make the two skip branches loud in CI while reading
  unchanged locally: prefix with `${GITHUB_ACTIONS:+::warning::}`. Keep the upload non-fatal.
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SentryConfig.swift:27-33`** — split nightly out of `"production"` via a
  testable helper (defaults to the real build facts so tests needn't fake a configuration):
  `defaultEnvironment(nightly: Bool = ReleaseChannel.isNightlyBuild, debug: Bool = isDebugBuild)`
  → `debug ? "development" : (nightly ? "nightly" : "production")`; keep the `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`
  override. Leave `releaseName` at the SDK default (nightly's version already carries `-nightly.<n>`).

Do **not** raise `appHangTimeoutInterval` — 2 s is the default and it caught a real bug.

## Step 1 — Cheap hex (behaviour-preserving)

**`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/Avatar.swift:54-55`** — replace `.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()`
with a nibble-table encode, `internal` (not `private`) so the equivalence test can reach it:

```swift
static func hexString<S: Sequence>(_ bytes: S) -> String where S.Element == UInt8
```

Append two bytes per input from a `[UInt8]("0123456789abcdef".utf8)` table into a `reserveCapacity(32)`
buffer, return `String(decoding: out, as: UTF8.self)` (stdlib, no Foundation). `%02x` is lowercase,
zero-padded, locale-free, so this is byte-identical by construction — **the gravatar URL must not
move**, and Step 5's test pins it.

## Step 2 — Build each `AvatarSubject` at most once

Add a `@MainActor private enum AvatarSubjectMemo` in `Avatar.swift` — a `[Key: AvatarSubject]`
dictionary keyed on `(VCSAuthor?, reviewer tag String?, pixelSize)`, cleared wholesale at a 512-entry
cap (no LRU: a miss is cheap after Step 1, and an eviction policy is code that needs its own tests).
`VCSAuthor` is already `Hashable, Sendable`, so no new conformances. Expose two factories mirroring
the two inits and switch all four call sites to them; leave the `init`s nonisolated and pure so the
existing `AvatarSubjectTests` stay non-`@MainActor`:

- `Views/HistoryPanel.swift:213` (row, 48px) · `Views/HistoryPanel.swift:458` (hover card, 54px)
- `Views/ChangesetDetailView.swift:156` (54px) · `Views/PullRequestPanel.swift:149-150` (reviewer branch)

`pixelSize` stays in the key — it's in the URL's `s=`/`size=`, so normalizing it would change the URL.

## Step 3 — Stop unrelated publishes rebuilding every row (the root-cause commit)

**`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/HistoryPanel.swift`**

- Add `@ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions` to `HistoryPanel` and hoist the selection fact
  into one private computed `selectedCommitID: String?` (the body of the deleted `isSelected`:
  `store.selectedTarget` → `sessions.focusedTab(for:)` → `case .changeset(let d)` → `d.commitID`).
  Inject at **`Views/ChangesPanel.swift:195`**: `HistoryPanel(model: store.commitHistory, sessions: store.terminals)`
  (`store.terminals` is a stable `let` on `AppStore`).
- `HistoryRow`: delete `@EnvironmentObject store` (`:157`), `@ObservedObject sessions` (`:160`) and the
  `isSelected` computed (`:346-353`); take `let isSelected: Bool` plus an **unobserved** `let sessions:
  TerminalSessions` (still forwarded to `DivergentSiblingRow`, which keeps its own subscription).
- Make the row elidable: conform `HistoryRow` to `Equatable` with a hand-written
  `==` over `commit`, `pushScope`, `isSelected` (synthesis is impossible — `theme`, four `@State`s, a
  closure), and wrap the use site in `.equatable()`. To make excluding `open:` provably safe, make
  `private func title(_:)` (`:70`) `static` and give the closure an explicit `[store]` capture list so
  it captures nothing per-pass. `HistoryRootRow` gets `: Equatable` (synthesized) + `.equatable()`.
- `@State` (hover, dwell popover, accordion) and `ThemeService`'s Observation tracking invalidate the
  row *directly*, past the equality gate — so hover, the popover, the accordion and theme repaints keep
  working. Verify the theme repaint by hand with History open (the one plausible regression).
- Leave `DivergentSiblingRow` as-is: at most a couple of rows, only while expanded.

## Step 4 — `LazyVStack` for the list

**`Views/HistoryPanel.swift:80`** — `VStack` → `LazyVStack`. `ForEach(model.commits)` keys on the
unique `commitID` (divergent copies live in the nested list), and the accordion comment at `:74-77` is
about SwiftUI *owning the scroll*, which is unchanged. `DiffViewer.swift:366`'s eager-on-purpose
comment is scoped to that view and doesn't generalize.

Side benefit: with `.loadRemoteAvatars` on, a 100-commit page currently fires ~100 gravatar
`AsyncImage` requests on load; after this only visible avatars are fetched.

Risk to check by running: a `LazyVStack` doesn't realize offscreen rows, so they leave the AX tree, and
`HistoryPushStateUITests` / `ChangesetDetailUITests` index `HistoryRow` by `boundBy:` and count rows.
The fixture seeds ~5 rows, which should all stay realized — if a deep index drops out, fix the *test*
(scroll before indexing), don't revert to eager.

## Step 5 — Cap the window at 1000 commits

**`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/HistoryModel.swift`** — `init(pageSize: Int = 100, maxWindow: Int = 1000, …)`
(injectable like `pageSize`, so tests can use `pageSize: 2, maxWindow: 4`):

- `loadMore()` — add `commits.count < maxWindow` to the guard, `load(limit: min(commits.count + pageSize, maxWindow))`.
- `refresh()` — `load(limit: min(max(pageSize, commits.count), maxWindow))`, so a grown window can't
  re-inflate past the cap on every ref-write refresh.
- Add `var atWindowCap: Bool { commits.count >= maxWindow }` (derived — no new `@Published`). Do **not**
  fold it into `reachedEnd`, which means "no older commits exist".
- **`Views/HistoryPanel.swift:106-124`** — when `!model.reachedEnd && model.atWindowCap`, render a
  `.secondary` note ("Showing the newest 1,000 commits") instead of a "Load more" that does nothing.

Own commit — it's the only user-visible change here.

## Step 6 — Tests

Unit (`make app-test`):

- **Extend `WorkroomAppTests/AvatarSubjectTests.swift`** — `hexString([b]) == String(format: "%02x", b)`
  for all 256 byte values (compares against the exact removed expression); hard-literal gravatar URLs
  for a couple of emails, plus the RFC 1321 anchors (`""` → `d41d8cd9…427e`, `"abc"` → `90015098…7f72`);
  memoized value `==` the plain-`init` value; 48 vs 54 are distinct keys.
- **New `WorkroomAppTests/HistoryRowInvalidationTests.swift`** (`@MainActor`) — the regression net.
  Add a `#if DEBUG static var bodyPasses` counter incremented at the top of `HistoryRow.body`, and make
  `HistoryRow` `internal` with the same documented rationale `HistoryCommitCard` already carries
  (`HistoryPanel.swift:404`). Host offscreen using the `NSWindow` + RunLoop-pump pattern from
  `PaneRenderingTests.swift:31-73` and the store setup from `HistoryLiveRefreshTests.activeHistoryStore`
  (`:66-86`). Assert: (a) a 200-commit model realizes far fewer than 200 rows; (b) **25 ×
  `pulsePaneActivity` → `bodyPasses == 0`** (fails on today's code, passes only with Step 3); (c)
  opening a changeset rebuilds ≤2 rows.
- **Extend `WorkroomAppTests/HistoryModelTests.swift`** — `loadMore` stops at `maxWindow`, `refresh`
  doesn't re-inflate past it, `atWindowCap` flips at the boundary, `reachedEnd` is not set by the cap.
- **New `WorkroomAppTests/SentryConfigTests.swift`** — `defaultEnvironment` truth table
  (nightly/production/development, debug wins).

XCUITest (own scheme; run per-method with `xcodebuild -only-testing:<Class>/<method>`, never the whole
suite):

- **Stress fixture** in `Core/UITestFixture.swift` — `-WorkroomUITestManyCommits <n>` (clamped, via the
  existing number coercion) generating *n* commits across ~7 distinct author emails, `root()` last.
  Leave the default 5-commit fixture **byte-identical** when the flag is absent — `HistoryPushStateUITests`
  depends on it exactly.
- **New `WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests.swift`** (reuse `HistoryPushStateUITests.openHistory`) —
  with 800 commits: realized `HistoryRow` count is `> 0` and `< 100`; clicking row 0 shows
  `ChangesetDetail` within 8 s (a hung main thread fails this by construction).
- **Re-run** `HistoryPushStateUITests` (all methods), the `openHistory` methods of
  `ChangesetDetailUITests`, and `InspectorAnimationUITests`.

## Verification

1. `make app-generate` (new files) → `make app-format` → `make app-build` → `make app-lint` →
   `make app-test`, all with the sandbox disabled (see the `building-macapp` skill).
2. Demonstrate the before/after ordering: `testTerminalSessionsPublishDoesNotRebuildRows` and the hex
   equivalence test must be **red on current code, green after**.
3. Run the XCUITest classes above per-method; eyeball the divergence accordion and a light/dark theme
   switch with History open (real mouse — synthetic hover lies).
4. Once by hand, Instruments (SwiftUI + Time Profiler) on a Nightly-config build with
   `-WorkroomUITestManyCommits 800`, History open, a terminal streaming output: show that
   `String.init(format:)` no longer appears under `ViewBodyAccessor.updateBody` and that `HistoryRow`'s
   View Body count stays flat while the terminal streams. No timing thresholds in CI (flake generator) —
   the `#if DEBUG` counters are the durable instrument.
5. After the next nightly ships, confirm a new event on WORKROOM-2B (if any) arrives with symbolicated
   `Workroom Nightly` frames, and that nightly events now carry `environment: nightly`.

## Deliberately not doing

- `MarkdownWebView.swift:118` (`css()`/`themeVars()`) — off the `ViewBodyAccessor` path, ~9 calls per
  theme change. Formatting floats is what `String(format:)` is for.
- `GhosttyApp.swift:250 hexColor` — dead, but deleting it is unrelated scope; noted for a cleanup pass.
- No LRU in the memo; no avatar identity pushed into `VCSCommit`/`HistoryModel` (wrong layer — would
  either store view-sized values or change the gravatar URL); no `selectedSiblingID` threading into the
  divergent subtree; no `pre`-vs-`stable` split by `environment` (same binary — a tag would be the
  honest expression, if wanted later).

```swift
static func hexString<S: Sequence>(_ bytes: S) -> String where S.Element == UInt8
```

Append two bytes per input from a `[UInt8]("0123456789abcdef".utf8)` table into a `reserveCapacity(32)`

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users

_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not

_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true

fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then

elif [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Writing Style (skip entirely if `EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse` appears in the preamble echo OR the user's current message explicitly requests terse / no-explanations output)

Applies to AskUserQuestion, user replies, and findings. AskUserQuestion Format is structure; this is prose quality.

- Gloss curated jargon on first use per skill invocation, even if the user pasted the term.
- Frame questions in outcome terms: what pain is avoided, what capability unlocks, what user experience changes.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).
* I err on the side of handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed.
* Bias toward explicit over clever.
* Right-sized diff: favor the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change ... but don't compress a necessary rewrite into a minimal patch. If the existing foundation is broken, say "scrap it and do this instead."

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

## Operationals
- [git-diff-rejects-pathspec-from-file] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-02)
  `git diff` and `git status` do NOT accept --pathspec-from-file (measured: `error: invalid option: --pathspec-from-file=-`), even though `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `git rm` and `git stash` all do. So a path-scoped diff cannot be fed paths on stdin and would need argv (E2BIG risk on large selections). Better technique for asking `which of these paths have staged content that a --only commit would discard`: run `git status --porcelain -z` UNFILTERED and filter in memory on the two status columns. X is HEAD->index, Y is index->worktree, so `MM` = partly staged and AT RISK, `M ` = staged and identical to disk (safe), ` M` = never staged (safe), `??` = untracked (safe). -z is required because a filename can contain a newline and git C-quotes non-ASCII names otherwise; a rename/copy entry (X in R,C) spends a SECOND NUL field on its old path, so a parser must consume it or the whole walk desyncs.
- [git-pathspec-glob-magic-after-double-dash] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-01)
  A git pathspec after `--` still honours GLOB MAGIC: `git add -- a[b].txt` also stages ab.txt, and a file literally named * stages the whole tree. `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing. Measured on throwaway repos. Fix: --pathspec-from-file=- with --pathspec-file-nul (paths taken literally, also removes argv E2BIG), or a :(literal) prefix per path. Related: `git commit -- <path>` implies --only and DISCARDS staged content for that path (data loss after git add -p), and --only alone cannot commit an untracked file, so a preceding `git add` is mandatory. jj is worse: paths are a fileset EXPRESSION language, a space hard-fails to parse, and a fileset matching nothing still creates an empty commit and exits 0.

The search results contain information about SwiftUI's @Observable dependency tracking system. Here are the key findings:

## Dependency Tracking with @Observable

One of the main advantages of using @Observable models in SwiftUI is that the framework can track individual property accesses. When a view reads a property in its body, it only needs to reevaluate when that property changes, rather than whenever another part of the model is updated.

## Skipped Body Observation Registration

All this works only if you read the value! If SwiftUI detects that your state's wrappedValue has changed but is not used/read in your body, it will completely skip its recomputation! This means SwiftUI has built-in optimization that prevents unnecessary view recomputation when observed properties aren't actually accessed in the view's body.

## EquatableView Usage

You can use the .equatable() modifier if you need more control. It can be applied to custom views that conform to the Equatable protocol. This allows for custom equality comparisons that can further optimize when views are recomputed.

## Property-Level Tracking

Views only re-render when the specific properties they read change, providing fine-grained dependency tracking that's more efficient than object-level observation with ObservableObject.

**Step 0 — scope challenge**

Existing code that already solves parts of this:
- Render caps are an established idiom, three places: `FileTreeModel.renderCap = 4000` (`Views/FilesPanel.swift:58-64`), `ChangesPanel.swift:703,849` (`renderCap = 200` + "Showing first N of M"), `CommitSheet.swift:66,173`. History is the one list with no ceiling. Cap should mirror that idiom, not invent a new one.
- `LibGit2.hexString` (`Core/LibGit2.swift:57`) exists but is `git_oid`-only, so the MD5 path can't reuse it. No generic byte-hex helper in the app, no `NSCache`/memo utility, and **zero** `.equatable()` / `EquatableView` uses — Step 3c introduces a new pattern here.
- Same defect shape in the Changes panel: `ChangedFileRow` (`Views/ChangesPanel.swift:434-437`) holds `@EnvironmentObject store` + `@ObservedObject sessions` for exactly one thing — `isSelected` (`:580`) — plus a `@Default` subscription per row. Bounded at 200 rows, so it's the same bug class at 1/5th the blast radius.

Counter-evidence to Step 4 found in-repo: `DiffViewer.swift:366-370` rejected `LazyVStack` because "a lazy stack caches a bad height estimate for not-yet-materialised wrapping rows". History rows are `lineLimit(1)` fixed-height, so that reasoning doesn't transfer — but the divergence accordion changes a row's height, which is the same hazard class.

Search check: offscreen `LazyVStack` rows are **not** in the AX tree for XCUITest on Xcode 14+ ([Apple forum](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/719444)), so `boundBy:` indexing needs a scroll — confirms the plan's flagged risk is real, not theoretical. Nested `LazyVStack` + active accessibility is a known hang ([thread 814208](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/814208)) — our nesting is `ScrollView > LazyVStack > VStack`, so it's clear, but worth not deepening. Observation is property-level and only tracks what a body **reads** ([fatbobman](https://fatbooman.com/en/posts/mastering-observation/)), which is why `.equatable()` can't hide a theme repaint — the invalidation targets the body attribute directly.

186	- **User flows:** What sequence of actions does a user take that touches this code? Map the full journey (e.g., "user clicks 'Pay' → form validates → API call → success/failure screen"). Each step in the journey needs a test.
187	- **Interaction edge cases:** What happens when the user does something unexpected?
188	  - Double-click/rapid resubmit
189	  - Navigate away mid-operation (back button, close tab, click another link)
190	  - Submit with stale data (page sat open for 30 minutes, session expired)
191	  - Slow connection (API takes 10 seconds — what does the user see?)
192	  - Concurrent actions (two tabs, same form)
193	- **Error states the user can see:** For every error the code handles, what does the user actually experience?
194	  - Is there a clear error message or a silent failure?
195	  - Can the user recover (retry, go back, fix input) or are they stuck?
196	  - What happens with no network? With a 500 from the API? With invalid data from the server?
197	- **Empty/zero/boundary states:** What does the UI show with zero results? With 10,000 results? With a single character input? With maximum-length input?
198	
199	Add these to your diagram alongside the code branches. A user flow with no test is just as much a gap as an untested if/else.

201	**Step 3. Check each branch against existing tests:**
202	
203	Go through your diagram branch by branch — both code paths AND user flows. For each one, search for a test that exercises it:
204	- Function `processPayment()` → look for `billing.test.ts`, `billing.spec.ts`, `test/billing_test.rb`
205	- An if/else → look for tests covering BOTH the true AND false path
206	- An error handler → look for a test that triggers that specific error condition
207	- A call to `helperFn()` that has its own branches → those branches need tests too
208	- A user flow → look for an integration or E2E test that walks through the journey
209	- An interaction edge case → look for a test that simulates the unexpected action
210	
211	Quality scoring rubric:
212	- ★★★  Tests behavior with edge cases AND error paths
213	- ★★   Tests correct behavior, happy path only
214	- ★    Smoke test / existence check / trivial assertion (e.g., "it renders", "it doesn't throw")

216	### E2E Test Decision Matrix
217	
218	When checking each branch, also determine whether a unit test or E2E/integration test is the right tool:
219	
220	**RECOMMEND E2E (mark as [→E2E] in the diagram):**
221	- Common user flow spanning 3+ components/services (e.g., signup → verify email → first login)
222	- Integration point where mocking hides real failures (e.g., API → queue → worker → DB)
223	- Auth/payment/data-destruction flows — too important to trust unit tests alone
224	
225	**RECOMMEND EVAL (mark as [→EVAL] in the diagram):**
226	- Critical LLM call that needs a quality eval (e.g., prompt change → test output still meets quality bar)
227	- Changes to prompt templates, system instructions, or tool definitions
228	
229	**STICK WITH UNIT TESTS:**
230	- Pure function with clear inputs/outputs
231	- Internal helper with no side effects
232	- Edge case of a single function (null input, empty array)
233	- Obscure/rare flow that isn't customer-facing

235	### REGRESSION RULE (mandatory)
236	
237	**IRON RULE:** When the coverage audit identifies a REGRESSION — code that previously worked but the diff broke — a regression test is added to the plan as a critical requirement. No AskUserQuestion. No skipping. Regressions are the highest-priority test because they prove something broke.
238	
239	A regression is when:
240	- The diff modifies existing behavior (not new code)
241	- The existing test suite (if any) doesn't cover the changed path
242	- The change introduces a new failure mode for existing callers
243	
244	When uncertain whether a change is a regression, err on the side of writing the test.

- [git-diff-rejects-pathspec-from-file] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-02)
  `git diff` and `git status` do NOT accept --pathspec-from-file (measured: `error: invalid option: --pathspec-from-file=-`), even though `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `git rm` and `git stash` all do. So a path-scoped diff cannot be fed paths on stdin and would need argv (E2BIG risk on large selections). Better technique for asking `which of these paths have staged content that a --only commit would discard`: run `git status --porcelain -z` UNFILTERED and filter in memory on the two status columns. X is HEAD->index, Y is index->worktree, so `MM` = partly staged and AT RISK, `M ` = staged and identical to disk (safe), ` M` = never staged (safe), `??` = untracked (safe). -z is required because a filename can contain a newline and git C-quotes non-ASCII names otherwise; a rename/copy entry (X in R,C) spends a SECOND NUL field on its old path, so a parser must consume it or the whole walk desyncs.
- [git-pathspec-glob-magic-after-double-dash] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-01)
  A git pathspec after `--` still honours GLOB MAGIC: `git add -- a[b].txt` also stages ab.txt, and a file literally named * stages the whole tree. `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing. Measured on throwaway repos. Fix: --pathspec-from-file=- with --pathspec-file-nul (paths taken literally, also removes argv E2BIG), or a :(literal) prefix per path. Related: `git commit -- <path>` implies --only and DISCARDS staged content for that path (data loss after git add -p), and --only alone cannot commit an untracked file, so a preceding `git add` is mandatory. jj is worse: paths are a fileset EXPRESSION language, a space hard-fails to parse, and a fileset matching nothing still creates an empty commit and exits 0.

**Section 1 — Architecture review**

**Issue 1** `[P1] (confidence: 9/10)` — the rows keep an `ObservableObject` even after the plan's fix. Motivating lines:

```
HistoryPanel.swift:157   @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
HistoryPanel.swift:160   @ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions
HistoryPanel.swift:346   guard let target = store.selectedTarget, let tab = sessions.focusedTab(for: target)
HistoryPanel.swift:488   @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore        // DivergentSiblingRow
HistoryPanel.swift:489   @ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions
HistoryPanel.swift:534   guard let target = store.selectedTarget, let tab = sessions.focusedTab(for: target)
```

Both row types use `store` and `sessions` for exactly one thing: comparing a commit id against the focused changeset tab. The plan removes observation from `HistoryRow` but keeps passing `sessions` in as an unobserved `let` and leaves `DivergentSiblingRow` fully observing. That leaves the hang one `@ObservedObject` re-添 away from returning, and no compiler or reviewer signal marks the `let` as load-bearing.

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 1: how far do we strip observation from the History rows? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-row-observation>

Project/branch/task: workroom, master; Step 3 of the App Hang fix (HistoryPanel.swift:157-160, :346-352, :488-489, :534-541).

ELI10: A row that watches TerminalSessions rebuilds every time a terminal's title or activity changes, which is many times a second while an agent streams. Both row types watch it only to answer "is my commit the one open in the focused tab?" — a single string comparison. If the parent computes the focused commit id once and passes it down as a plain string, no row watches anything, and the question is answered identically. The plan half-does this: it fixes the outer row but still hands it a live TerminalSessions object as an unobserved property, and leaves the divergent-sibling row watching as before.

Stakes if we pick wrong: an unobserved `let sessions` reads like an oversight, so the next person adds `@ObservedObject` back and the 2-second hang returns with no test failure unless the invalidation test exists. The sibling row keeps rebuilding on every pulse whenever an expander is open.

Recommendation: A — one value passed down, zero observation in either row; it is strictly less code than the plan and removes the landmine instead of documenting it. Maps to "explicit over clever" and "smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change".

Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10, C=6/10

**Issue 2** `[P2] (confidence: 9/10)` — the symbol fix can break the nightly build. Motivating lines:

```
nightly.yml:141      run: brew install xcodegen create-dmg protobuf
release.yml:62       run: brew install xcodegen create-dmg getsentry/tools/sentry-cli protobuf
release.sh:105-107   # Optional and non-fatal ... a symbol-upload hiccup must never block shipping
release.sh:110-118   if [ -n "${SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN:-}" ] ... if command -v sentry-cli ... else echo "note: ..."
```

`release.sh` degrades gracefully in both directions, but the brew line does not: copying release.yml's pattern into an unattended cron job means a Homebrew tap hiccup fails the nightly before it ever archives, and nobody notices except that the `nightly` release asset silently goes stale.

**Issue 3** `[P2] (confidence: 8/10)` — after this lands, the next hang is still undiagnosable from the report alone. Motivating lines:

```
SentryConfig.swift:40     options.enableAppHangTracking = true
SentryConfig.swift:48     options.tracesSampleRate = 1.0
SentryConfig.swift:51-54  options.configureProfiling = { $0.sessionSampleRate = 1.0; $0.lifecycle = .trace }
```

`.trace` lifecycle means a profile exists only while a sampled transaction is open. The app opens none for idle SwiftUI updates (Sentry's SwiftUI instrumentation needs explicit `SentryTracedView`), so WORKROOM-2B arrived as one stack sample with unsymbolicated app frames — which is why this session had to infer the culprit from code reading rather than read it off a profile. The plan's `#if DEBUG` counters don't ship, so a recurrence produces the same single sample.

ELI10: An app-hang report gives you one snapshot of the main thread at the moment the watchdog fires. content.text:
**Section 4 — Performance review**

Two positives worth recording, since they change how much the rest matters:

- With `LazyVStack`, `ForEach` only builds views for realized indices, so `HistoryPanel.body` observing `sessions` (required by 1A) costs ~visible rows per pulse, not N. The parent-observation concern I expected here dissolves — the equality gate and the struct churn are both O(visible).
- The 1000-commit cap earns its place on the VCS side, not the layout side. Prior learning applied: **history-eager-focus-is-a-full-vcs-read** (9/10) — `refresh()` is repo open + revwalk + `GitGraph.unpushed` range walk over `max(pageSize, commits.count)`, fired per ref write by the metadata watcher.

**Issue 8** `[P2] (confidence: 7/10 — medium: whether Gravatar's 404 is cacheable is unverified)` — `LazyVStack` makes avatar loading repeat:

```
Avatar.swift:48-50   /// `d=404` makes Gravatar 404 (not serve an identicon) when it has no image …
Avatar.swift:106     AsyncImage(url: url, transaction: Transaction(animation: .easeOut(duration: 0.15)))
HistoryPanel.swift:212-213   AvatarStack(subjects: commit.authors.map { AvatarSubject(author: $0, pixelSize: 48) }, size: 16)
```

Today every row loads once because the eager stack builds them all once. Under lazy realization, scrolling a long history re-creates `AsyncImage` each time a row comes back into view, and a `404` response is typically not stored by `URLCache` — so an author with no Gravatar re-requests on every pass through the viewport.

questions.question:
D11 — Issue 8: mitigate repeated avatar requests introduced by lazy realization? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-perf-avatar-image>

Project/branch/task: workroom, master; Step 4 interaction with Avatar.swift:48-50/:106.

ELI10: Avatars are fetched from Gravatar with a flag that makes it answer 404 when it has no picture for that email, and the app then draws coloured initials. Successful images get cached by the system's HTTP cache; a 404 usually does not. Right now that costs one request per author per session because every row is built once. After the lazy-stack change, rows are built each time they scroll into view, so a team of authors without Gravatars means a small request storm every time you scroll the log. Remembering "this URL had no image" for the rest of the session removes it.

Stakes if we pick wrong: repeated 404s on every scroll — wasted network, and the initials chip flickering through its loading phase each time. Both are small individually and both are new, caused by this change.

Recommendation: B — remember failed URLs for the session. It is about ten lines in the file we are already editing, and it closes a regression our own change introduces.

Completeness: A=6/10, B=9/10, C=8/10

options.label: 8A) Accept it — measure first
options.description:
Ship the lazy stack as-is; revisit if network noise or flicker is visible.

✅ Keeps the diff strictly on the hang path, and a 404 round trip to Gravatar is cheap and off the main thread
✅ Avoids adding session state whose invalidation rules nobody has thought through yet
❌ Knowingly ships a new repeated-request pattern for the common case of a repo whose authors have no Gravatar

options.label: 8B) Session-scoped negative cache (recommended)
options.description:
Main-actor Set<URL> of URLs that failed; AvatarView skips AsyncImage for a known-failed URL and draws initials directly. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

✅ One request per missing avatar per session instead of one per scroll pass, and the initials chip stops flickering through a load phase
✅ Ten lines in Avatar.swift with no eviction question: a URL that 404'd stays 404 for the session, and a relaunch re-checks
❌ Session state means a Gravatar added mid-session will not appear until relaunch, and it is a second piece of view-layer caching to keep honest

options.label: 8C) Cache successes too
options.description:
Add a small in-memory image cache keyed by URL, plus the negative set.

✅ Removes decode and re-request work for successful avatars as rows recycle, not just the 404 path
✅ Makes long-history scrolling visually stable regardless of how the system HTTP cache behaves
❌ Duplicates what URLCache already does for cacheable responses, and an unbounded image cache is a memory question this change does not need to open
